chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from a man from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you raise your head from the bowing (ruku'), then straighten your back, for there is no prayer for one who does not straighten his back."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on straightening the back after bowing in Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* emphasizes the physical integrity of the prayer posture, linking the validity of *salat* to the complete straightening of the spine (*iqamat al-sulb*) after rising from *ruku'*. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a key evidence for the requirement of *itmi'nan* (tranquility/stability) in postures, ensuring the worshipper is fully present and stable before proceeding to the next act of worship. The ruling underscores that haste or instability in transitioning between postures compromises the ritual's completeness.
